note: Inbound prompt screening and outbound tool-execution blocking are separate host capabilities. A host that intercepts a prompt does not necessarily allow refusing it, and a host that can refuse a tool call does not necessarily expose the prompt. Each field below records what the named host version can do, not what Little Canary wishes it could do.

hosts.name: Claude Code

inbound.interception_point: after the prompt is submitted, before the turn starts
inbound.runtime_evidence: Verified against Claude Code 2.1.261 for release 0.3.7. Not re-exercised at runtime by this certification.

caveats: Screens the submitted prompt only. Tool results, tool arguments, and file contents read during the turn are never screened.
A request body over 64 KiB is rejected by the loopback server with HTTP 413 and is therefore not screened at all.

hosts.name: OpenCode

inbound.interception_point: when a new user message is received, before the model request
inbound.runtime_evidence: OpenCode 1.18.32 loaded the local plugin in an isolated configuration. An `opencode run` invocation with a synthetic flagged verdict made one request to the loopback Little Canary test service and printed `Little Canary: Prompt flagged; OpenCode continued.` before the host's model request failed on a dummy API key. Offline package tests cover clean, flagged, unsafe, degraded, unavailable, and invalid-endpoint results. This certifies hook dispatch and warning delivery, not detector efficacy with a live model.

tool_result.interception_point: after a tool runs, before its text result reaches the next model request
tool_result.runtime_evidence: The five-file npm package archive was installed in an isolated OpenCode 1.18.32 profile. A local mock provider requested a read of a synthetic file, and a local screening service returned pass, unsafe, and unavailable outcomes in separate runs. Each run reached a second model request. Pass and unavailable forwarded the original read text; unsafe forwarded only the replacement notice. Unavailable emitted a warning. This proves string-result hook dispatch and transformation for this host version, not detector efficacy or other tool-result shapes.

caveats: The stable chat.message hook has no typed input-rejection result. An unsafe service verdict warns but cannot stop the OpenCode turn.

Current user-message text parts, string tool results, and text items or embedded resource.text in raw MCP results are screened. Known advisory flags remain visible when screening coverage is degraded. The MCP content path is backed by OpenCode 1.18.32 source and an offline adapter test, not an installed-host run. Earlier conversation, attachments, tool arguments, and non-text results are outside this adapter. A file read is screened only after the tool returns its text.

The tool-result hook cannot undo tool execution. Rejected string results are replaced before the next model request; service failures and bodies over the server's 64 KiB limit warn and continue with the original text. OpenCode V2 plugin APIs have not been certified for this package.

hosts.name: Codex CLI

inbound.interception_point: after the prompt is submitted, before the turn starts
inbound.runtime_evidence: Install route exercised: `codex plugin marketplace add <checkout>` then `codex plugin add little-canary@hermes-labs` reports `installed, enabled` at 0.3.8 and copies hooks/hooks.json plus the adapter into the plugin cache. Interception itself was NOT observed: in a headless `codex exec` run against an isolated CODEX_HOME the hook did not execute, no hook-trust state was recorded, and the prompt proceeded to the model call with no warning. Codex gates hook execution behind an explicit trust approval that a non-interactive run cannot give.

caveats: Codex does not run a hook until its source is trusted. Until a maintainer approves the hook interactively, the plugin is installed and enabled but screens nothing, and Codex says nothing about it.
The same limits as the Claude Code route apply: submitted prompt only, 64 KiB body ceiling.

hosts.name: Gemini CLI

inbound.runtime_evidence: Verified against Gemini CLI 0.32.1 for release 0.3.7; see README 'Gemini CLI extension'. Not re-exercised at runtime by this certification.

caveats: Denies one agent run at its pre-agent boundary. Tool calls made inside an allowed run are not screened.

hosts.name: OpenClaw

inbound.interception_point: before model submission on OpenClaw paths that dispatch before_agent_run; verified with agent --local
inbound.runtime_evidence: Verified with OpenClaw 2026.9.5 on Node 26.1.0: local-path plugin install and runtime inspection reported typedHooks.before_agent_run; `openclaw agent --local` blocked a synthetic unsafe response from a loopback test service before reaching a local fake model, while a benign response reached that fake model. OpenClaw 2026.9.6 on Node 24.21.0 installed the packed package in an isolated profile; runtime inspection reported one loaded before_agent_run hook after the documented conversation-access grant. Host-dispatched block made no fake-model call, while pass, degraded, and unavailable-service controls reached the fake model. These used deterministic loopback test services, not a live canary. The isolated `agent exec` path bypassed this hook in 2026.9.5 and is outside claimed coverage.

caveats: Screens only event.prompt; the handler does not separately inspect event.messages history, tool calls, tool results, or files.

OpenClaw documents before_agent_run for embedded and CLI runners, but `openclaw agent exec` bypassed plugin hooks in the verified runtime; use a path that dispatches this hook. It is not a Codex or Copilot input gate.
Requires the operator to run the Little Canary loopback service. The plugin passes through when service checks fail or report degraded coverage.
The service rejects HTTP request bodies over 64 KiB; this plugin passes those runs through unscreened.
The non-bundled plugin needs hooks.allowConversationAccess enabled for its entry.

hosts.name: Pi

inbound.interception_point: after input is received and before agent processing
inbound.runtime_evidence: Pi 0.87.1 loaded the local package in an isolated PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR profile. A `pi --print --no-session --offline` invocation with an HTTP loopback test service returning safe:false emitted the Little Canary block notice and exited without model output. Package unit tests cover pass, flagged advisory, degraded, unavailable-service, and invalid-endpoint controls. This certifies the host's input-handling boundary, not detector efficacy with a live model.

caveats: The extension screens only input event text. Pi runs registered extension commands before input, while skill and prompt-template expansion happens afterward, so those paths or additions are not screened.
It does not separately inspect prior conversation, tool outputs, file reads, or images.
The recommended advisory service policy flags without refusing input. Only an explicit unsafe verdict from a blocking service policy makes this extension handle the input before the model.
Service errors, malformed verdicts, and over-limit request bodies pass through with a warning.

hosts.name: OpenAI Agents SDK

inbound.runtime_evidence: Offline tests exercised against openai-agents 0.22.0; the SDK tripwire is the deny channel. No live model call is involved in the guardrail decision.

caveats: Only user-message text is screened by the input-guardrail adapter. The separate examples/document_agent.py tool explicitly calls documents.guard_document before returning fetched text; it does not automatically cover other tools or non-text content.
SDK input guardrails run only for the first agent in a chain.

hosts.name: Hermes Agent

inbound.interception_point: before the model call, context injection only
inbound.runtime_evidence: Verified on 2026-09-23 against Hermes Agent 0.21.4 in an isolated Python 3.13 environment: installed the pinned Git subdirectory with its Python dependency, enabled little-canary, and Plugin Doctor reported successful import and three hook registrations. Offline hook tests show that a structural BLOCK annotates the user turn and vetoes downstream tools while an unrelated turn remains allowed. Host turn assembly still appends hook context to the original user message; pre_llm_call has no deny channel. No live model call was made.

caveats: This is the one host where Little Canary blocks outbound tool execution rather than inbound prompt delivery.
A BLOCK verdict withdraws the turn's tool authority. It does not stop the prompt from reaching the model.

hosts.name: GitHub Copilot CLI

inbound.interception_point: after the user submits a prompt
inbound.runtime_evidence: Artifact-certified, not runtime-certified. UserPromptSubmittedHookOutput exposes modifiedPrompt, additionalContext, and suppressOutput and no decision field; only PreToolUseHookOutput carries permissionDecision allow/deny/ask. See docs/host-evidence/copilot-cli-1.0.84-5-hook-outputs.d.ts. The Copilot CLI was not installed on this machine, so no run was exercised.

caveats: Copilot cannot refuse an inbound prompt at any hook. A userPromptSubmitted hook can rewrite or annotate the prompt; the prompt still reaches the model.

Copilot's file-configured hooks use a different manifest than Claude Code and Codex: `.github/hooks/*.json`, `version: 1`, camelCase event names, and `bash`/`timeoutSec` keys. The `plugins/claude-code` hook manifest is not loadable by Copilot.
Little Canary ships no Copilot artifact. A Copilot marketplace listing of this plugin is an install route for other hosts, not evidence of Copilot prompt screening.
